insights.insight: The protocol settles verified purchase receipts at ~$0.10 per confirmation (148 sats) against ad tech CPA rates of $5–$150 for probabilistic attribution — a 50–200x cost delta that is structural, not a promotional rate.

Verified receipts now span grocery, big-box, pharmacy, discount, warehouse club, automotive, peer-to-peer resale, and online marketplaces — meaning the signal set reflects the full consumer spending stack, not a skewed sample of digital-native buyers.

insights.topic: CVS Pharmacy entry signals health category unlock
insights.insight: CVS Pharmacy entered the top-brand list at 30 receipts in the 14-day window, the first pharmacy/drugstore chain to appear — health and wellness purchase data is now entering the verified receipt pool, a category historically difficult to attribute in cookieless environments.

The 14-day window accounts for 29.0% of all-time protocol GMV, up sharply from 22.6% in the prior reading — the dataset is compounding into present activity, not diluted by a long historical tail, which increases signal freshness for targeting use cases.

Combined Amazon receipts (115 across two DKIM variants) are effectively tied with Walmart (116) at the top of the brand stack — two-channel capture within a single vendor ecosystem is producing redundant confirmation signals that strengthen attribution confidence.

Gas and convenience receipts average ~$127 per transaction across 193 receipts in the 14-day window — the highest resolved per-receipt average in the dataset, suggesting high-value fuel or fleet purchases are entering the pool and may represent a distinct buyer segment worth isolating.
